summary.intent: Execute Phase 37 (parallel-batch-upload-pipeline) using the GSD wave-based orchestration workflow, running 2 plans across 2 waves with subagent parallelization.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (plan 37-01: SDK batch upload pipeline) completed successfully with 10 unit tests and 3 commits. Wave 2 was not yet reached; the session ended after merging the worktree branch back into the feature branch.

repo: Plan 37-01 implements `uploadFiles()` on `CipherBoxClient` with p-limit concurrency (max 3 concurrent), re-reads folder metadata after uploads to avoid stale-children races, and does a single folder IPNS publish.
Plan 37-02 (Wave 2) handles Web Worker encryption and `useDropUpload` rewire — depends on Wave 1's SDK method.
workflow: GSD executor agents run in isolated git worktrees; after completion the orchestrator must explicitly merge the worktree branch back into the feature branch before proceeding.
Merging worktree branches can produce conflicts in STATE.md and config.json; the worktree version of STATE.md was used to resolve the conflict.
Spot-checks (SUMMARY.md existence, key files, test files, recent commits) are used to verify agent completion before advancing waves.
The stale auto-chain flag in gsd-tools config must be cleared at init when `--auto` is not passed, to prevent unwanted auto-advance from prior interrupted runs.

friction: Merging the worktree branch back required multiple bash steps and produced a merge conflict in STATE.md that needed manual resolution.
Working tree had local changes (STATE.md, config.json) that had to be stashed before the merge could proceed.
